newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says two HK activists board Japan vessel.
newsitem.headline: Japan says two HK activists board Japan vessel.

text.p: Two activists aboard the flagship of a Taiwan-Hong Kong flotilla challenging Japan's claim to islands in the East China Sea jumped from their ship onto a Japanese coastguard boat on Monday, a coastguard spokesman said.

The two activists have not been arrested or detained and will be returned to their 100-tonne vessel called the "Protect-the-Diaoyus" as soon as possible, the spokesman for the Maritime Safety Agency, or coastguard, told Reuters.

The Protect-the-Diaoyus is leading a 20-strong flotilla from Taiwan and Hong Kong which is challenging Japan's sovereignty over an island chain called the Senkakus in Japanese and the Diaoyus in Chinese.
The names of the two activists were not available.
The coastguard has mobilised about 60 patrol boats to prevent the flotilla from approaching the disputed island chain.
In Tokyo, top government spokesman Seiroku Kajiyama warned that the coastguard would seize ships and arrest protesters if they tried to land on the uninhabited islets.
